explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/921: for k ≥ 4 and f_k(n) the largest m such that some n-vertex graph of chromatic number k has all odd cycles longer than m, is f_k(n) ≍ n^{1/(k−2)}? (proved by Kierstead–Szemerédi–Trotter). The Lean statement gives, for each k ≥ 4, constants c₁, c₂ > 0 such that eventually (a) some G on Fin n with χ = k has every odd cycle length > c₁ n^{1/(k−2)}, and (b) every G on Fin n with χ = k has an odd cycle of length ≤ c₂ n^{1/(k−2)}. These two halves are exactly f_k(n) ≫ n^{1/(k−2)} and f_k(n) ≪ n^{1/(k−2)} (graphs with χ ≥ 3 always have odd cycles, so (b) is meaningful). Faithful.
